rows: Here's a test. Rub two things together for long enough and something gets hot. Think about that.
I am not a gimmick when I hit the mat. I am a force, the same as a storm.
Pressure builds up when you hold back. I would not hold back if I were you.
Slow things down all you like. Energy will find a way out.
The crowd came to see something they cannot explain. Give them the spark.
I am here, and it is not an accident.
I am an attraction. The reactions in this building are proof of that.
Look at the pose. It is a warning, not a costume.
You say I am a gimmick. Watch what I do, then say it again.
Blows build up heat. You will feel it before you know what it is.
Risk, friction, pressure. You have all three to think about.
A slow pace is a pressure valve. I will be the one opening it.
The people paid for something new. Give them the experiment.
You want the crowd to notice you. Good luck with the static.
Pride in your {strength}, a good spark. That makes sense, because it is a real force in this match.
I have been thinking about your {strength}. I think it creates a useful kind of pressure.
You stayed calm. Lovely. Let us see how the heat behaves.
Fair enough, like a current. We both know the reactions will decide it.
I could explain that in detail. I would rather let the match explain it.
One fall, one proper result. Give me the chance and I will show you the reaction.
On the mat, the friction gets interesting. Stay close.
Grounded or standing, I keep moving. You cannot hold the energy in.
Stay where you are if you think you can contain it.
That was a fair reaction. Now let us see the reaction.
Heat gives you an answer. Your silence does not. Feel the answer, then give it.
Fair point. Let us turn it into something useful.
Fair enough, the static is gone. I take that and I will use it at the bell.
I will be in there giving everything I have. The rest is physics.
I am ready to give the crowd something they cannot explain, and I mean that.
Whatever happens, something will change in that ring.
The result is still open. I like it that way.
I have an idea. Let us see whether it works.
I can feel the temperature rising in this room. That tells me nothing about whether the charge is true.
You're asking for an observation, not a reaction. I can't give you one that proves it.
Then let that particular spark go out. We've still got a match to light up.
That's clearer. Let the heat come from the wrestling, not from a guess about you or me.
Watch what happens when the pressure builds and neither of us can back away. That's the test.
The crowd can see which of us turns all that energy into something that actually wins a fall.
An accusation is static, not a result. What can we demonstrate when the pressure builds in the ring?
Treat the match as the experiment, not a verdict on the rumour. What can the people observe?
You've built a circuit around my {strength}. Let's see where the current goes when you try to cut it off.
Knowing how to contain my {strength} on paper won't tell you what happens when the pressure rises.
Point taken. A theory needs a result before we call it a fact.
Fair. Let's keep the speculation out of the circuit and see what happens under pressure.
Time builds pressure. It doesn't tell you where the next release is coming from.
Your years are a force in this contest. So am I.
Experience teaches me to feel the pressure building before a position breaks.
I've learned to redirect the force instead of meeting every impact head-on.
You studied the last storm. The pressure is building differently this time.
Your notes show where the force went last time. Let's see where you direct yours when I change mine.
I study how pressure travels through a hold, then practise redirecting it before it peaks.
My preparation is finding the point at which resistance becomes useful movement instead of wasted force.
